Before first contact, randomized dose changes only independently driven competing capture clocks with predictable path susceptibilities, under dose-linearity, no-interference and calibrated relative-dose premises. Each integrated susceptibility A_j is finite almost surely; no finite mean or maximum-rate bound is assumed. A_j has inverse-dose units: interpreting it as exposure time requires calibration of b_j. The post-contact extension requires q to cover relevant first contacts conditionally and a persistent tag; q is a design premise, not acquired data, and q<1 leaves a residual in the actual response.","costs":"The finite-net procedure has no model-uniform upper bound on experiments or dyadic stages. Its dose net may be exponential in the number of channels, and the smallest realizable dose can limit resolution. Imperfect first-contact coverage leaves residual outcome freedom; physical instrument and calibration costs are unmeasured. The 12 arms by 12,000 draws (144,000 total) are synthetic only and establish no physical acquisition.","obstruction":"The selected source return lacks interception_operators.json and interception_contact_operators.json, so this intake does not replay the fit or certify the reported dual/contact calculations. Before the first probe hit, a nonnegative dose vector c changes only independently driven competing capture clocks with predictable path susceptibilities b_j(t), under the stated dose-linearity and no-interference contract. If each integrated susceptibility A_j is finite almost surely (without a finite-mean or maximum-rate bound), then the no-hit outcome subprobabilities are K_b(c)=E[1{B=b} exp(-c·A)]. A weak mixed-dose challenge acquires the common continuity modulus L(h)=K_hit(h,...,h).
